claims.text: Substrate lattice mismatch modulates residual interfacial strain in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi thin films.
Residual interfacial strain modulates magnetoelastic coupling during the magnetostructural transformation.
A lower substrate lattice mismatch produces less residual strain in the film.
Reduced residual strain minimizes strain-induced tetragonal distortion.
Reduced strain-induced lattice distortion decreases the energy barrier for the magnetostructural phase transition.
A lower transformation barrier produces a more abrupt magnetostructural transformation.
A lower transformation barrier improves transformation reversibility and reduces hysteretic losses.
A high-mismatch substrate increases residual strain and the transformation barrier.
An increased transformation barrier broadens hysteresis.
Films on low-mismatch substrates will exhibit a sharper magnetocaloric response than films on high-mismatch substrates.
Films on low-mismatch substrates will exhibit narrower hysteresis than films on high-mismatch substrates.
Films on low-mismatch substrates will exhibit more reversible magnetic-cooling cycles than films on high-mismatch substrates.
A high-mismatch as-deposited baseline is likely to have broader hysteresis and a less pronounced magnetocaloric effect.
MgO is an example of a low-lattice-mismatch substrate and sapphire is an example of a high-lattice-mismatch substrate for the proposed FeMnNiGeSi film.
There is a nanoscale film-thickness regime in which substrate-induced strain dominates the response.
Heat-transfer rate limitations are relevant to the cycling conditions and cycle frequency.
